content.text: No minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, or volume restriction is imposed on Ono anywhere in the agreement. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: (a) Ono shall have the right (but not the obligation) to Manufacture and/or package, or engage a Subcontractor to Manufacture, Ono's requirements of particular Materials (e.g., Ono's requirements of Drug Substance or Ono's requirements of Drug Product of a particular Product) related to any Product for the Ono Territory.
input.rationale: The supply architecture in Article IX meets our preferred position: there is no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, binding minimum forecast, or shortfall penalty on Ono. Section 9.4(a) expressly gives Ono the right "but not the obligation" to Manufacture (or have a Subcontractor Manufacture) its own requirements, and Section 9.4(b) gives Ono the "right to obtain" commercial requirements from Array — Array's supply duty (9.4(b)(i)) runs one way in our favour, covering "Ono's reasonable requirements". Payment obligations are limited to the upfront fee, achievement-based milestones and royalties on actual Net Sales (Art. VI), i.e. usage/ordered-volume based only. The only "shortfall" reference (p0430) is a year-end royalty reconciliation true-up, which is the true-up mechanic the playbook prefers, not a volume penalty. Ono's diligence duties (Sections 5.1(b)(iii), 8.1(a)) are Diligent Efforts commercialization standards, not volume commitments. The Section 8.2 exclusivity-of-efforts covenant is a competing-product restriction, mutual in scope, and is addressed under the exclusivity rule rather than double-flagged here. No redline required.
